Label-to-value gap consistent: vertical gap between each number and its label, across the deck
Parallel baselines align: first-line baselines of side-by-side cards
Spacing hygiene in the source text: double spaces, a space before ? ! : ; or %, tabs, zero-width characters (U+200B–U+200D, U+2060, U+FEFF) and soft hyphens (U+00AD)
Tracking consistent per role across the deck: manifest letter-spacing (em) per role
Vertical rhythm between blocks: the headline-to-body gap and the body-to-source gap
pass: headline to body 0.8–3.0 × the body line pitch; body to source ≥ 1.0 × the body line pitch †
evidence: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.8 (ref) (paragraph spacing ≥ 1.5 × line spacing, AAA).

test: Spacing spot-check: a reviewer views 3 random words per slide at 100% (1080 px) and at 200%
pass: no visible holes, touches or uneven pairs

test: Minimum line length: characters on each non-final body line
evidence: Butterick (45–90 for documents); V-C09 caps slides at 40.

test: Lines per body block: line count of each body block
evidence: ARC Bronze (> 2 lines = body text with stricter contrast needs); V-G01 (≤ 30 words).

test: Headline lines: line count of each headline
Text lines per content slide: total text lines on the slide, excluding the footer and source
No body runts: the last line of each body block (V-C11 covers headlines only)
pass: ≥ 2 words and ≥ 25% of the block's longest line width †

test: Rag quality: left-aligned blocks of 3 or more lines
pass: every non-final line ≥ 65% of the longest, and no run of 3 lines that each shrink by more than 10% (a "staircase") †

test: No weak line endings: the last word on each line
pass: headlines have 0 lines ending in a, an, the, of, to, in, on, at, by, for, and, or, with or your; body blocks have at most 1 per block †

test: No hyphenated breaks anywhere: automatic end-of-line hyphens in any text (V-C25 covers headlines only)
evidence: Butterick (hyphenation belongs with justified text, and slides are not justified).

test: No justified text: text alignment
pass: 0 elements with text-align: justify. Pixel cross-check: no block whose non-final lines end within 1 px of each other while the word-gap coefficient of variation exceeds 0.3

test: Paragraph spacing: the gap at a paragraph break inside a card
pass: baseline-to-baseline across the break ≥ 1.5 × the line pitch within the paragraph

test: Even leading: baseline-to-baseline distances within a block
evidence: Butterick (one line spacing per text block). This catches mixed inline sizes and fallback glyphs that push lines apart.

test: Balanced centered headlines: centered headlines of 2–3 lines
pass: the shortest line ≥ 60% of the longest †

test: One headline case style per deck: case style of each headline
pass: all sentence case or all title case †

test: Typographic punctuation: source strings
pass: 0 straight quotes or apostrophes outside URLs, 0 double hyphens, 0 "..." (use …), ranges use an en dash, multiplication uses ×
evidence: Butterick (curly quotes; apostrophes point down; hyphens are not dashes).

test: Hanging indents in lists: wrapped lines in bulleted and numbered lists
pass: the left ink edge of each wrapped line within ±3 px of the first line's text start (not the bullet) †

test: Emphasis restraint: emphasized runs (a weight or color change) per element
No underlines: underlined runs
pass: 0 (image text is not clickable, and an underline signals a link) †

test: Breaks at phrase boundaries: whether each headline line is a meaningful phrase, with no noun phrase split and no verb cut from its object
Lining figures: digit heights within each number
pass: max ÷ min ≤ 1.03. Oldstyle figures vary in height and descend

test: Dollar-sign size and position: $ height ÷ digit height, and its top alignment when reduced
pass: 0.55–1.15; if below 0.90, the top of the $ is within 3% of digit height from the digit tops †

test: Dollar-sign spacing: ink gap between the $ and the first digit, and the source string
pass: gap 0.02–0.12 × digit height, with no space character in the string †

test: Percent sign: % placement and size
pass: no space between the number and the %; % height 0.90–1.10 × digit height †
evidence: convention (US news style; not verified this session).

test: True minus sign: negative values
pass: U+2212 (or U+2013), never U+002D; the rendered bar ≥ 0.5 × the median digit width; one order (−$2.40) across the deck

test: Numbers never break across lines: number tokens, including $, %, ¢, sign, and attached abbreviations (/mo, /yr, K, M, B)
pass: every token on one line, 100% of the time. A split "$2." / "90" misstates a price †

test: Thousands separators visible: commas in numbers
pass: a separate component at master and at SIM1, with ≥ 2 px clearance from the neighboring digits †

test: Decimal point visible: decimal points in amounts and percentages
pass: a separate component with area ≥ (0.10 × digit height)² at master and at SIM1 (and at THUMB for slide-1 hero numbers), and T-O03 returns the point. A lost point turns $2.90 into $290 †
evidence: Tesseract FAQ (ref) (marks below about 8 px are dropped as noise); Erdmann 2022.

test: Even digit spacing in hero numbers: ink gaps between consecutive digits
pass: max ≤ 1.5 × median, and median ≤ 0.12 × digit height †
evidence: OpenType tnum (ref) (equal advance widths leave gaps around a narrow "1"); V-C13 calls for tabular figures only in stacked numbers.

test: Stacked numbers aligned: right edges (or decimal points) of amounts stacked in one column
pass: within ±3 px. This extends V-H11's receipt rule to every stacked comparison and makes it measurable †

test: Large-number abbreviations: abbreviated amounts
pass: one style per deck ("$1.2M" or "$1.2 million"), uppercase K/M/B, no space †

test: Ranges: numeric ranges
pass: en dash with no spaces, the $ on both ends ("$5–$10"), and one % style per deck

test: Multiplication sign: multiplier claims
Leading zero: decimals below 1
Cents formatting: amounts with cents
pass: two decimals ($2.50, never $2.5), and ¢ and $0.xx are not mixed for the same kind of value within a deck †

test: Digits distinct in the numeral face: pairwise IoU of the rendered glyph pairs 3/8, 5/6, 6/8, 1/7 and 0/8 at the smallest numeral size used
No monospace numbers: fonts used for numbers
pass: post.isFixedPitch = 0; tabular alignment comes from the text face's 'tnum'
evidence: Sasidharan & Dhanesh, AMCIS 2008 (monospace rated less trustworthy than serif or sans on a simulated bank site).

test: Hero-number finish: a reviewer at 200% checks for lining digits, even stroke color, no novelty digit shapes, and a proportionate $ and %
No slivers: components of the face and bevel masks
pass: exactly 1 face component per digit, and 0 bevel components smaller than 0.2% of the digit's area or thinner than 3 px †

test: No shading creases: luminance outliers in bevel and side-wall regions
pass: 0 clusters larger than 20 px with |L* − 7×7 median| > 25 †. Flipped normals show up as dark creases

test: Even bevel: visible bevel width along the face contour
pass: 4–12% of digit height, with a coefficient of variation ≤ 0.25. A pinched bevel signals self-intersection †

test: Face reads against its surroundings: front-face median against the local background, and against the side walls
pass: Lc ≥ 60 against the background and ΔL* ≥ 8 against the side walls †
evidence: APCA Easy Intro (Lc 60 for content text; Lc 15 for discernible non-text).

test: Pose keeps digits legible: camera yaw, pitch and roll relative to the numeral
pass: yaw ≤ 30°, pitch ≤ 20°, roll ≤ 10°, and the foreshortened face width ≥ 85% of frontal (cos 30° ≈ 0.87) †

test: Highlights don't erase the digit: specular area on the front face
pass: pixels at L* ≥ 95 cover ≤ 15% of the face, and none bridges a counter †
evidence: V-D13 (at most 1% pure white across 3D pixels).

test: Edge sharpness after delivery: 10–90% rise distance of glyph edges at SIM1
Ringing around text: mosquito noise in a 1–4 px ring around the glyphs at SIM1
Chroma bleed on colored text: colored glyphs (core C* > 20) at SIM1
pass: mean ΔE00 against REF1080 in a 2 px ring ≤ 4, and the hue of glyph cores shifts by ≤ 5° †
evidence: Erdmann 2022 (colored edges suffer most); Chroma subsampling.

test: Thin strokes survive two encodes: component and hole counts per glyph at SIM2
No blocking in text areas: blockiness inside text boxes at SIM1
pass: mean |ΔY| across 8 px block boundaries ÷ mean |ΔY| between adjacent interior pixels ≤ 1.3 †. Complements V-A08 (master)

test: Grayscale anti-aliasing: color fringes on the edges of neutral text at master
pass: P95 chroma C* ≤ 6 on edge pixels (mask alpha 0.1–0.9) where both text and background are neutral (C* < 5) †. This catches subpixel (LCD) text rendering in the headless browser
evidence: Chroma subsampling (color detail is what JPEG discards first).

test: No sharpening halos: a halo brighter than the background next to dark glyph edges at master
pass: P99 overshoot ≤ 3 L* against the BG plate in a 1–3 px ring †

test: Exact text after delivery: per-element OCR at SIM1 for headlines, numbers, the CTA URL, source lines and disclaimers
Two OCR engines agree: tesseract and EasyOCR on master and SIM1
pass: both match. If only one matches, flag the slide for Judge review rather than failing it †

test: Digits-only read of every number: each number, 3D numerals included, OCR'd with a character whitelist
pass: exact match at master and SIM1, plus THUMB for slide-1 hero numbers
evidence: Tesseract ImproveQuality (PSM 7; dictionaries off for non-dictionary text).

test: OCR confidence: tesseract word confidence from image_to_data
pass: every word ≥ 85 at master and ≥ 70 at SIM1 †. A correct but low-confidence read signals marginal legibility

test: No clipped glyphs: glyph ink lost to overflow, tight line boxes, or card and slide edges
pass: 0 px lost, and no glyph pixel within 1 px of its clip rect
evidence: V-B09 (covers only cuts at the slide edge); Tesseract ImproveQuality (text needs a border).

test: Padding inside cards: distance from any glyph ink to the edge of its container
Line breaks as designed: rendered line count and the word ending each line, against the content spec
pass: equal when the spec sets breaks; otherwise within the T-L02/T-L03 limits †
evidence: convention; catches reflow caused by a fallback font or a width change.

test: No stray text: OCR PSM 11 on FINAL outside the manifest boxes, logos and declared 3D numerals
No template leaks: manifest strings plus full-slide OCR
pass: 0 matches for {{, }}, ${, undefined, null, NaN, [object, lorem, ipsum, TODO, TBD, XXX, "Headline here" or "$X"
evidence: none needed; a leaked placeholder is an embarrassing failure.

test: No fallback glyphs or tofu: each rendered glyph against the declared font's reference rendering
pass: SSIM ≥ 0.85 for every glyph, 0 .notdef boxes, and one platform font per element as CDP reports it †. This extends V-A12 (PDF) to JPGs

test: Every element is present: whether OCR finds each manifest element inside its bbox
pass: 100% †. Catches text hidden behind a 3D object or panel, or rendered transparent

test: Reading order: element order by position (top to bottom, then left to right within a row) against the manifest's narrative order
pass: equal †. This is a Script proxy for V-E10

test: Text coverage on promoted slides: union of OCR word boxes, each dilated by 0.25 × box height, ÷ image area, on any slide used in a Meta ad
Text coverage on the organic hook slide: as T-P01, on slide 1 of organic posts
Read-aloud panel: 5 raters, each holding their own phone at a normal distance, read each slide's body text and source line aloud from the SIM1 file
pass: ≥ 4 of 5 read with no errors within 10 s

test: Number-at-a-glance panel: each slide is shown for 1.5 s on a phone, and raters write down the hero number
evidence: MIT AgeLab; Readability Matters 2020 (millisecond differences in glance legibility are significant).

test: Approved families only: the platform fonts used for each text node
evidence: Chrome DevTools Protocol (ref); Monotype/CITE 2019 (fragmentation lowers trust).

test: No script, handwriting, monospace or novelty faces: font metadata
pass: 0 faces with PANOSE bFamilyType 3 (hand-written) or 4 (decorative), and 0 with post.isFixedPitch = 1

test: Text face has a large x-height: OS/2 sxHeight ÷ unitsPerEm of the text face
Required glyphs and features: the text face's cmap and GSUB tables
pass: cmap contains U+2212, U+2013, U+2014, U+2018/2019, U+201C/201D, U+2026, U+00D7 and U+00A2; GSUB has 'tnum' and 'lnum' (or the face's default figures are lining)

test: I, l and 1 are distinct: pairwise IoU of I, l and 1, and of 0 and O, at body size
pass: IoU ≤ 0.80 for the I/l/1 pairs and ≤ 0.90 for 0/O, or a disambiguating stylistic set is enabled †

test: No synthesized bold or italic: requested weights and styles against the real instances
pass: every requested weight and style exists (a static file, or a value inside the variable font's axis range), and font-synthesis is none †

test: Optical sizes used: font cut or opsz value by size, when the family offers them
pass: the Text cut (or opsz at text size) for h < 98 px, and the Display cut for headlines of 187 px or more

test: Paired faces match on a shared line: two families set on the same line
pass: x-height ratios within ±0.04 and baselines within 1 px †
evidence: Legge & Bigelow 2011 (x-height as the size metric).

test: Weight bands by role: computed font-weight per role
pass: body and spot text 400–600, headlines 600–800, numbers 500–800 †
evidence: W3C Understanding 1.4.3 (thin fonts render fainter); APCA Easy Intro (minimums depend on weight).

test: No distorted type: text transforms
pass: scaleX = scaleY within ±0.5%, no skew, and rendered glyph aspect within ±3% of the reference †
evidence: none found; faux-condensed type is a common sign of amateur work.

test: No outline or fake-3D effects on 2D type: stroke and shadow styles on text
pass: 0 elements with -webkit-text-stroke above 0 or with 2 or more stacked text-shadows; approved 3D numerals are exempt
evidence: W3C Understanding 1.4.3 (wide outlines count as halo, i.e. background).

test: A second family has one job: roles that use the second family
pass: if two families are used, the second appears in at most 1 role (for example numerals only) †

test: Trust panel: 5 raters rate slide 1, with the logo masked, on "looks like a trustworthy financial company" from 1 to 5
Render-pass export: every slide render also writes the pass set listed in the header
pass: all 9 artifacts exist; every image is exactly 2160x2700 (or 2x that if supersampled); the `id` pass has no blended colors
evidence: inference. Most checks below need passes, because comparing passes gives the most reliable detectors (see Takeaway). three.js Scene docs (accessed 2026)

test: Rejected-slide regression set: the checker runs on the stored Nov 11 rejected renders
pass: it fails every one of them on the intended check: "6" and "$" (R-D01/R-D02/R-A08), arrow, coin and "?" seams (R-N01/R-N07), "?" cut by a card (R-G02/R-Z05) and the shadow-camera line (R-S02)

test: three.js upgrade gate: any change of `THREE.REVISION` re-renders the golden set and runs all R-checks before production use
evidence: users reported shadow pixelation in r182; there `PCFSoftShadowMap` was deprecated and the renderer "does not automatically switch" to its replacement — three.js forum, "Shadow Pixelation Issue in Three.js 0.182.0" (2025–26). Other r182 upgrade threads have titles about transparency and point-light shadow regressions (titles only seen) — three.js forum (2026).

test: Assets loaded before capture: fonts, the environment map, textures and the typeface JSON have all loaded before the frame is captured
pass: `document.fonts.status === 'loaded'`, every loader's onLoad has fired, and the loading manager reports 0 pending items

test: Calibration set for statistical thresholds: every threshold labeled "calibrated" (IQA scores, CLIP margins, noise) is fit on SVPay's own approved slides
pass: ≥ 20 approved slides in the calibration set, refit at least every 30 days
evidence: BRISQUE and NIQE are built on natural-scene statistics from photographs (see section 5), so absolute scores on flat synthetic graphics are not meaningful without a local baseline (inference).

test: Edge-profile width: the width over which a glyph silhouette edge rises from 10% to 90% (catches both jaggies and FXAA or depth-of-field smear)
evidence: FXAA is a post-process filter on the final image, so it softens all edges including detail — NVIDIA, FXAA white paper (Lottes) (2009).

test: Supersampled reference agreement: compare the shipped frame with a high-sample reference near silhouettes
pass: in a 4-px band around silhouettes, mean ΔE ≤ 1.5 and P99 ≤ 6
evidence: three.js TAA example (accessed 2026); LearnOpenGL, Anti Aliasing.

test: Specular sparkle (broken highlights) on bevels: bevel highlights form continuous streaks, not dotted, aliased fragments
pass: ≤ 10 isolated highlight specks (≤ 4 px each, more than 3 px from a larger highlight) per glyph
evidence: specular aliasing on high-curvature, high-gloss geometry is a known real-time problem — Möller, Haines, Hoffman et al., Real-Time Rendering, 4th ed., ch. 9 (2018).

test: Shadow-edge stair-step residual: the shadow boundary is a smooth curve, not a zig-zag at the scale of shadow-map texels
pass: RMS distance between the shadow's 0.5 contour and its smoothed version ≤ 0.30 px
evidence: jagged shadow edges come from fixed shadow-map resolution — LearnOpenGL, Shadow Mapping; r182 pixelation reports — three.js forum (2025–26).

test: Text kept out of screen-space anti-aliasing: HTML text is composited after any FXAA or SMAA pass and is never filtered by it
pass: SSIM ≥ 0.98 between each text box in the final image and the same text box rendered on its own
evidence: FXAA filters every pixel of the final image — NVIDIA FXAA white paper (2009).

test: Anti-aliasing kept through post-processing: if EffectComposer is used, its render targets keep multisampling, or a supersampling/TAA pass replaces it
pass: `composer.renderTarget1.samples >= 4`, or the pass list contains SSAA or TAA
evidence: `WebGLRenderTarget` has a `samples` option for MSAA — three.js WebGLRenderTarget docs (accessed 2026).

test: Glyph topology (Euler number): each rendered glyph silhouette has the same number of holes as the font glyph. This catches counters filled by a self-intersecting bevel, strokes cut by cards and broken geometry
pass: Euler number equals expected for 100% of glyphs (for example "0", "6", "9" → 0; "8" → −1; "1", "2", "3", "5", "7" → 1; "4" depends on the font)
evidence: scikit-image measure API (accessed 2026); the Nov 11 "6" and "$" defects.

test: No aliasing in high-frequency textures: the holographic or diffraction pattern and grain textures don't alias into moiré
pass: in sheen regions, spectral energy above 0.4 cycles/px, after subtracting the flat-background grain spectrum, is ≤ 5% of total AC energy
evidence: texture minification needs mipmaps and filtering to avoid aliasing — Real-Time Rendering, 4th ed., ch. 6 (2018).

test: Thin features survive: the narrowest visible part of each glyph (stroke junctions, the inside of a counter, terminals) stays wide enough to read
pass: ≥ 6 px wide at 2160 px, measured as 2 × the maximum of the distance transform along the medial axis
evidence: inference. Platform downscaling to 1080 px halves every feature (see R-A11).

test: Floor texture filtering: textures on surfaces seen at grazing angles (the floor) use mipmaps and maximum anisotropy
pass: `tex.anisotropy === renderer.capabilities.getMaxAnisotropy()` and `minFilter` is a mipmap filter

test: Shadow camera covers every receiver: the directional light's orthographic shadow camera contains every caster's footprint plus a margin, and the visible receiving floor is either fully inside it or fades out before its edge
pass: footprint plus 10% inside the frustum, and receiver opacity is 0 at least 5% before the frustum edge (or the floor is entirely inside)
evidence: sampling outside the light frustum gives false shadows, and the light frustum should be fit to the scene — LearnOpenGL, Shadow Mapping; Microsoft Learn, Common Techniques to Improve Shadow Depth Maps (accessed 2026); Nov 11 shadow-camera-line rejection.

test: Shadow-frustum edge line detector: no straight, faint line appears in the shadow pass or the background outside designed elements
pass: 0 straight segments longer than 10% of the slide width with a step of 0.01–0.2 in `shadow` (or 0.3–6 L* in the high-passed beauty) outside the masks for casters, cards and text
evidence: Nov 11 rejection (a faint stair-stepped line across the background was the shadow-camera edge); LearnOpenGL.

test: Shadow on/off difference stays inside the predicted footprint: turning shadows off changes only pixels inside the casters' predicted shadow region
pass: no connected region larger than 50 px with |ΔL*| > 0.5 outside the footprint (dilated by penumbra width + 20 px)
evidence: inference from the shadow geometry in Kee et al., ACM TOG (2013). This catches frustum edges, stray casters and floor self-shadowing.

test: Shadow acne energy ratio: lit glyph surfaces have no shadow-induced striping
pass: high-pass energy with shadows on ÷ with shadows off ≤ 1.15 on pixels with N·L > 0.2 that are fully lit
evidence: acne is a striped pattern caused by depth-map resolution — LearnOpenGL; `normalBias` "can be used to reduce shadow acne" — three.js LightShadow docs (accessed 2026).

test: Contact or clear float (no peter-panning, no ambiguous hover): a glyph either touches the floor with a contact shadow or floats clearly above it
pass: gap h ≤ 0.2% of glyph height counts as contact, and then the shadow in the 0–6 px band under the contact edge reaches ≥ 80% of the glyph's peak shadow, with no lit gap wider than 2 px. A gap h ≥ 3% counts as floating. Anything from 0.2% to 3% fails as ambiguous
evidence: bias can make shadows look detached ("peter panning") — LearnOpenGL. The ambiguity band is an inference: a near-touch reads as a defect rather than intent.

test: Shadow texel density: one shadow-map texel, projected onto the floor at the glyphs, covers less than one output pixel
pass: ≤ 1.0 px per texel if `radius ≥ 2`; ≤ 0.5 px if `radius = 1`
evidence: map resolution and frustum fit decide edge blockiness — LearnOpenGL; Microsoft Learn, shadow depth maps.

test: Shadow type valid for the installed revision: the shadow-map type is not deprecated and is not the hard-edged BasicShadowMap
pass: on r182 or later with WebGLRenderer, type is `PCFShadowMap` (or baked or accumulated shadows), never `PCFSoftShadowMap` or `BasicShadowMap`
evidence: "`PCFSoftShadowMap` is now deprecated. Use `PCFShadowMap` which is now soft as well," and this applies only to WebGLRenderer — three.js forum r182 (2025–26).

test: No variance shadow maps (VSM) for stills: VSM is not used
evidence: VSM blurs the map (`blurSamples`, default 8) — three.js LightShadow docs. Real-Time Rendering documents VSM light bleeding where shadows overlap — RTR 4th ed., ch. 7 (2018). The three.js Renderer-constants docs also state that with VSM all receivers also cast shadows, which would make the floor and cards casters — three.js constants (not re-fetched in this session; verify).

test: Contact hardening: shadow penumbrae widen with distance from the contact point, as real soft light does. Fixed-radius PCF gives a uniform blur that reads as CG
pass: penumbra width (10–90% ramp) at the farthest 20% of the shadow ≥ 1.5× its width at the nearest 20%
evidence: percentage-closer soft shadows (PCSS) estimate penumbra size from the distance between blocker and receiver — NVIDIA, Percentage-Closer Soft Shadows (Fernando) (2005).

test: No banding in the penumbra: soft shadow ramps show no visible steps
pass: CAMBI ≤ 3 on a crop around each shadow, and the R-B03 contour-run count is 0 inside penumbrae
evidence: "High values [of radius] will cause unwanted banding effects in the shadows" — three.js LightShadow docs; CAMBI "around 5" is slightly annoying — Netflix CAMBI doc.

test: Shadow density suits a light design: shadows are soft and airy, with a darker contact core
pass: the darkest floor shadow is L* ≥ 55, and the contact band is ≥ 5 L* darker than the shadow's middle
evidence: inference. V-D06 (slide mean L* ≥ 85) and V-I25 (no near-black shadows) set the light-design context; contact occlusion is the strongest grounding cue — Real-Time Rendering, ch. 11 (ambient occlusion) (2018).

test: One shadow per glyph per light: a baked contact shadow, a second shadow-casting light or a stale shadow does not double the shadow
pass: shadow lobes per glyph equal the number of shadow-casting lights (normally 1)
evidence: a scene lit by one source must have mutually consistent shadows — Kee et al., ACM TOG (2013).

test: Shadow and shading direction agree with the stated light: in the image plane, the direction from glyph to shadow agrees with the projected light direction, and so does the shading gradient across the front faces
pass: shadow offset angle within 15° of the projected light; front-face shading gradient within 30° of it
evidence: shadows and shading must be explainable by one light — Kee et al. (2013). This is internal 3D consistency; V-I02 compares the 3D layer with the HTML layer.

test: Glass cards cast lighter shadows: frosted cards cast no shadow, or a shadow at most half as dark as a glyph's and tinted, never an opaque grey slab
evidence: three.js transmission and shadow interplay is limited (transmission samples only opaque objects) — three.js forum, 2023. Physical plausibility is an inference.

test: Shadow is current: the shadow was rendered after the final transforms
pass: the measured shadow centroid is within 1% of slide width of the centroid predicted from the scene
evidence: shadows depend on `autoUpdate` and `needsUpdate` — three.js LightShadow docs (accessed 2026).

test: Depth precision: the camera's near and far planes keep enough depth precision
pass: `far/near ≤ 1000`, and near ≥ 1% of the camera-to-subject distance (or `logarithmicDepthBuffer: true`)
evidence: z-fighting comes from limited depth-buffer precision; remedies are moving the near plane outward and avoiding near-coplanar surfaces — LearnOpenGL, Depth testing (accessed 2026); `logarithmicDepthBuffer` option — three.js WebGLRenderer docs.

test: No coplanar overlapping faces: no two meshes have overlapping triangles in the same plane (for example a decal on a card, or a floor and a shadow catcher at the same height)
Z-fighting jitter test: a tiny camera move or near-plane change does not swap which object is visible
pass: 0 pixels change object ID, excluding a 2-px band around ID boundaries

test: ID-pass speckle: no salt-and-pepper interleaving of two object IDs (the still-image signature of z-fighting)
pass: 0 speckle pixels outside the 3-px silhouette band

test: Glyph–card clearance: no 3D glyph passes through a glass card's plane inside the card's rectangle
pass: all glyph vertices that project into the card rectangle (+5%) lie on one side of the plane, with |distance| ≥ 3% of glyph height
evidence: Nov 11 rejection (a "?" cut by a glass card).

test: Glyph–glyph clearance: separately extruded glyphs never interpenetrate
pass: minimum 3D distance between any two glyph meshes ≥ 2% of glyph height
evidence: Nov 11 rule (each glyph extruded on its own with even gaps); trimesh.

test: No glyph sinks into the floor: glyph meshes stay out of the floor
pass: no vertex lies more than 0.2% of glyph height below the floor plane
evidence: inference. Penetration hides the contact edge that R-S06 relies on.

test: No near-plane clipping: no visible mesh is cut by the camera's near plane
pass: every vertex is at least 1.05 × near in front of the camera

test: Glass cards have real thickness: cards are thin boxes or rounded boxes, not zero-thickness planes, so their edges render and nothing coplanar can fight with them
evidence: inference, plus NN/g's note that a stroke creates an "illusion of thickness" that makes glass read as an object — NN/g, Glassmorphism (2024).

test: Unexpected-edge (seam) detector: every sharp edge inside a glyph matches a real geometric crease, a shadow terminator or a highlight boundary
pass: total length of unexplained step edges ≤ 2% of the glyph perimeter, and no single unexplained segment longer than 20 px
evidence: Nov 11 rejection (seams on arrows, coins and question marks).

test: Normal continuity on smooth surfaces: no small normal discontinuities (3–20°) inside surfaces meant to be smooth; that range is the signature of faceting and seams
pass: pixels with a 3–20° jump to a neighbor ≤ 0.2% of glyph pixels
evidence: unjoined vertices give faceted shading on TextGeometry, fixed by merging vertices and recomputing normals — three.js forum, smooth shading on TextGeometry (2022).

test: MikkTSpace tangents when normal maps are used: any mesh with a `normalMap` (for example micro-variation under V-I03) has MikkTSpace tangents
pass: the `tangent` attribute exists and comes from `computeMikkTSpaceTangents`
evidence: "inconsistent tangents may lead to subtle visual issues in the normal map, particularly around mirrored UV seams" — three.js BufferGeometryUtils docs (accessed 2026).

test: UV-seam continuity: textured materials (holographic, roughness) show no color step where UVs jump
Smooth reflections on front faces: the flat front faces of numerals reflect a smooth environment, with no blotches, blocky low-resolution environment texels or noise
pass: residual standard deviation of L* after a σ = 8 px high-pass ≤ 1.0 above the grain estimate
